stdin.note: Built-in commands are entered either in in-game chat by a player with the right permission group, or at the dedicated server's console. The Linux build (./colonyserver.x86_64 -batchmode -nographics +server.world "<world>") takes the command line directly; the Windows wrapper colonyserverdedicated.exe has its own shell (quit / list / start_server / stop_server / send) and requires each game command to be prefixed with "send ", e.g. "send /blacklist add 76561198156320300". Commands keep their leading slash and are case sensitive. No RCON and no HTTP admin API; LinuxGSM's colserver reaches the console through tmux.

notes: Vanilla Colony Survival has no kick, no player-list and no broadcast command. The wiki's full command page (Cheats / Colony Commands / Server Commands / Permissions / Debug Commands) contains no /kick, /ban, /unban, /say, /announce, /players, /online or /list, and the widely used ColonyCommandsMod exists precisely to add /kick, /ban and /online - which is strong evidence the base game lacks them. Blacklisting is the only vanilla moderation action. The wiki gives the full form as "/blacklist [ clear | add {player} | remove {player} ]": with no argument it prints the current blacklist, and "/blacklist clear" empties it. UNVERIFIED SIDE EFFECT: no source read states whether blacklisting DISCONNECTS a player who is currently connected. The community thread is titled "Blacklisting/kicking a player" and the asker wanted a griefer removed, but no reply confirms an active session is dropped - so do not treat blacklist as a kick without testing. DISAGREEMENT: hosting knowledge bases (Legion Hosting, listed in sources) publish "/kick [PlayerName]", "/ban [PlayerName]", "/unban [PlayerName]", "/players" and "/say [Message]" for Colony Survival. Nothing official or community-sourced supports those and they look copied from a generic template, so they are NOT recorded here. IDENTIFIER RISK: the wiki and the Steam command guide both write the argument as {player} / <player name>, and /setgroup is documented as taking either USER_NAME or STEAM_ID, while community practice for blacklisting is to paste the SteamID64 (the forum thread's advice is literally "go /blacklist add >paste the numbers<" after looking the id up); the permission file gamedata/savegames/<world>/permissionusers.json keys users as "1.<steamid64>" (1 = the Steam network-id type). SteamID64 is recorded because it is the only form that can work for a player who is not currently connected, but a connected player's name may also be accepted - this is the main reason confidence is low. No ban-file path is recorded because no source states where the blacklist is persisted. The Colony Survival Wiki is a community Fandom wiki, not publisher-hosted docs, so both wiki sources are kind "wiki". Steam app 748090 is the free Colony Survival Dedicated Server; the game itself is app 366090.
